description: A 6-member Karachi-based team with backgrounds in AI/ML, software development, and full-stack engineering... including members from AgenticEra Systems and other academic/professional backgrounds. We've placed Top 18/626 at Google's AI Seekho National Hackathon. For "Flame in Freefall," we're building an AI-powered dashboard turning NASA's microgravity combustion research into clear fire-safety insights. Team is complete.
summary:
FlameLedger helps researchers answer a practical question: which NASA combustion experiments are relevant to a proposed spacecraft or lunar cabin? Our dashboard lets users enter cabin conditions, compare experiments side by side, and trace each result to the original report. It shows which conditions are similar, which differ, and which were never reported.

The lunar walkthrough compares Saffire VI, an orbital combustion test with a similar atmosphere, with LUCI, an experiment that simulated lunar gravity under different atmospheric conditions. Seeing both studies together makes it easier to understand what each can tell us and where more testing is needed. FlameLedger turns scattered research into evidence that teams can inspect, compare, and export.
details:
Team Qubit built FlameLedger for the Flame in Freefall challenge to make NASA’s combustion research easier to use. A researcher evaluating a proposed cabin may need to open several reports just to determine whether two experiments used comparable oxygen concentrations, pressures, gravity levels, or airflow. FlameLedger brings those conditions together and keeps the original sources within reach.

Users can select a lunar or ISS-like cabin scenario, or enter their own conditions. The dashboard organizes studies around fire prevention, detection, and suppression and explains how each experiment relates to the selected environment. Users can compare runs side by side, open the report and table behind a result, inspect the coverage map, and export the evidence as a CSV.

We fine-tuned the text encoder of Google DeepMind’s EmbeddingGemma 2 to retrieve relevant combustion research. We used Gemma 4 12B to generate synthetic search questions from NASA Technical Reports Server passages, then trained the encoder to retrieve the passages those questions referred to. FlameLedger combines this semantic search with BM25 keyword search. In our notebook benchmark, the fine-tuned hybrid retrieved the labeled passage among the first five results for 94% of 150 synthetic test questions, compared with 91.3% for the base model using the same hybrid approach. The dashboard separately ranks experimental runs using documented test conditions and flags missing information.

Our lunar walkthrough shows why that distinction matters. Saffire VI-2 tested SIBAL fabric at 31% oxygen and 54.1 kPa in orbital microgravity. LUCI tested the same type of fabric under simulated lunar gravity in air at normal pressure. Saffire offers a closer match on atmosphere, while LUCI offers a closer match on gravity. The comparison helps researchers see what each study contributes and where further testing is needed.

We built the backend with Python, FastAPI, SQLite, and NumPy, and the frontend with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The pixel-art research console gives the dashboard a clear visual identity. Every comparison keeps the source, test conditions, and review status visible so researchers can judge how much weight to give the evidence.
